clue.text: Where people are barely noticeable

parts.note: 'barely' looks like 'hardly', but read literally it means 'in the nude': a place where everyone goes about unclothed

explanation.definitionFit: A naturist camp is a settlement where residents wear no clothes at all.

clue.text: Brad's ready for a punch

parts.note: a brad is a small thin nail
set means prepared, ready

explanation.surface: Someone called Brad is squaring up to throw a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brad' looks like a man's name, but it is a kind of small nail; 'for' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This tool is a small steel punch used to drive nail heads below a wood surface.

clue.text: Car in which daughter injured a miler

indicators.note: injured suggests the words a miler are damaged and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A runner's daughter was hurt in a car accident involving a middle-distance athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges A MILER into AIMLER, placed after D.
explanation.definitionFit: A British luxury motor marque, so a make of automobile.

clue.text: Crazy snooker player could do this

definitions.meaning: an eccentric or mad person, or describing one
to put backspin on the cue ball in snooker is to screw it

explanation.surface: A snooker player has gone mad at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric is a madcap oddball; separately, a backspin shot in snooker is called a screw.

clue.text: Put an end to cold comfort

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ease means comfort, relief

explanation.surface: Someone wants to stop the cold comfort they are being offered.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or stop something is to bring it to a finish.

clue.text: See about man joining

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'See about man joining' (7): LO round IVOR gives LIVORO with no word for the N and no definition for the Italian port; the clue appears cut short in the OCR and no source found gives the rest.

clue.text: Cold wind cutting into negative woman-right

indicators.note: cutting into means the word for right slices into the middle of the words before it

parts.note: no is a negative reply
her is a pronoun standing for a woman

explanation.surface: A biting wind is slicing into a woman who has just been refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting into' has RT go between NO and HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong chilly gale blowing from the north, especially in the southern US.

clue.text: Exercise choice in building material to make bridge neat

indicators.note: in means the choosing word sits inside the material word

parts.note: sand is used in building, for mortar and concrete
to exercise choice is to pick
a span is a bridge or its arch

explanation.surface: A builder picks a material to make a tidy bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PICK inside SAND, giving SPICKAND; 'to make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for spotlessly tidy and clean.

clue.text: One gets in power kitchen implement comparatively dear

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: gets in means the numeral for one enters the middle of the kitchen word

parts.note: a ricer is a kitchen gadget that presses cooked potato into fine strands
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A powerful kitchen gadget turns out to cost more than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' puts I into RICER to make RICIER, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: More expensive, the comparative of costly.

clue.text: Conflicting notice on poetry

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A notice posted on a poem is in dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in an across clue AD simply comes before VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary or opposing, as in adverse opinions working against one another.

clue.text: One knowledgeable about cricket, say?

parts.note: cricket suggests the bat-and-ball game, but here it is the chirping insect, and 'say' marks it as one example of the creatures studied

explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies insects, of which the cricket is one.

clue.text: Grasping thing about sea changes which creates precedent

indicators.note: about means the grasping word goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a claw is a gripping part

indicators.note: changes indicates the letters of sea are reordered

explanation.surface: A crab's claw grips at a sea that keeps altering, setting an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges SEA into ASE; 'about' puts CLAW around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Law built from judges' earlier rulings, each decision binding later courts.

clue.text: To hear's possible in this

indicators.note: possible suggests one possible arrangement of the letters of the first words

explanation.surface: Somewhere you can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' signals an anagram of TO HEARS, and the whole clue also defines the range within which you can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The range within which sound can be picked up by a listener.

clue.text: Growth of tares getting out of hand?

indicators.note: getting out of hand suggests the letters of tares run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Weeds in a field are spreading uncontrollably.
explanation.walkthrough: Tares are weeds, so a gardener expects 'growth' to describe them running riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like flower is a plant, and plants are growths.

clue.text: One going off with broken arm to get an X-ray

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of going have gone bad and been rearranged
broken means the letters of arm are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone goes to hospital with a broken arm to have it X-rayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns GOING into NGIOG and 'broken' turns ARM into RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiograph of blood vessels taken after injecting a contrast dye.

clue.text: Georgia seen with licentious one, a revolutionary type

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
ribald means coarse, lewd
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone from Georgia is seen out with a debauched revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen with' is a link. The definition doubles as a type of biscuit named after the Italian revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe of that name led the Italian unification; the name is also a currant biscuit.

clue.text: Rev up, getting into this?

parts.note: rev up suggests revving an engine, but here a Rev is a clergyman getting dressed, putting on the white neckband of his office

explanation.definitionFit: The stiff white band worn round a clergyman's neck.

clue.text: Fare from Italy for one escaping coaching disaster

indicators.note: disaster suggests the remaining letters are thrown into chaos and reordered
escaping means the letter for one gets out of the word coaching

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: A coaching session goes wrong, and one person gets away for an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping' takes A out of COACHING to leave COCHING, which 'disaster' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Small potato dumplings, an Italian dish.

clue.text: Strange character seeing old theologian's angle

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An odd person shares an old theologian's point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'angle' looks like a viewpoint but is the verb to fish; 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric, someone peculiar.

clue.text: Peg to get good result? Almost

indicators.note: almost means the phrase for succeeding is not quite finished, losing its final letter

parts.note: to do well is to get a good result

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether pegging away brings success, and gets the answer: nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; DO WELL loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden pin used to join two pieces of timber.

clue.text: Movement required from player having nap on top of arch

indicators.note: on top of means in this down clue the nap word sits above the arch word

parts.note: nap is soft fluffy surface fibre, like down
a bow is an arched shape

explanation.surface: A player naps perched on the top of an archway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nap' looks like a snooze but means soft fluff; 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke of a violin bow from frog to tip, which a string player makes.

clue.text: Bizarrely odd instances of delay below dam

indicators.note: below means in this down clue the delay letters come under the dam word

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river

indicators.note: odd instances of means take the first, third and fifth letters of delay

explanation.surface: Strange delays keep happening downstream of a dam.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of DELAY are D, L, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: In a strange, uncanny manner.

clue.text: Poland's relatively unusual ploughman, homeward bound?

parts.note: PL is the international code for Poland
odder means more unusual, comparatively strange

explanation.surface: A peculiar Polish farmhand walks home from the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition echoes Gray's Elegy: 'The ploughman homeward plods his weary way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow trudger, as Gray's farm worker who trudges home at dusk.

clue.text: Man said to have received message

definitions.meaning: radio operators say this word to confirm a message has been received

explanation.surface: A man is reported to have got the message.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male name, and also the radio reply meaning understood.

clue.text: Breach of law in endless indulgence producing angry cry

indicators.note: in means the broken law letters go inside the shortened indulgence word
endless means the indulgence word loses its last letter

parts.note: a binge is a bout of indulgence

indicators.note: breach of suggests law is broken and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Breaking the law in a never-ending spree leads to a furious shout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts BINGE to BING; 'Breach of' turns LAW into AWL, which 'in' places inside it; 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud shouting or howling in rage or distress.

clue.text: At Birmingham venue, leader is showing affection

parts.note: the NEC is the National Exhibition Centre, a large exhibition and concert venue near Birmingham, England
a king is a leader

explanation.surface: At an event in Birmingham, the head of state is being affectionate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissing and cuddling, an amorous display.

clue.text: Urges politicians to keep current party

indicators.note: to keep means the politicians word holds the current and party words inside it

parts.note: Libs is short for Liberals, politicians
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Politicians push to retain the governing party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts I and DO inside LIBS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual drives or desires, the plural of a Freudian term.

clue.text: Lines of illumination seen at Canary Wharf?

parts.note: light is illumination
railway lines, tracks

explanation.surface: Bright rows of lights are on show at a London business district.
explanation.walkthrough: Canary Wharf is a business district in London's Docklands, served by the Docklands Light Railway; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail system of lighter trains, as in the Docklands network serving that district.
